import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Run an agent on a cron expression. Schedules are their own resource, so one agent can have many, each with its own input and timezone. Manage them at `/v1/schedules`. Scheduled runs appear in the dashboard like any other run.

## Cron expressions

Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Each field accepts `*`, lists, ranges and `*/N` steps:

```text
# ┌─── minute (0-59)
# │ ┌─── hour (0-23)
# │ │ ┌─── day of month (1-31)
# │ │ │ ┌─── month (1-12)
# │ │ │ │ ┌─── day of week (0-7, Sun=0 or 7)
# │ │ │ │ │
# * * * * *

0 9 * * 1-5     # every weekday at 9:00 AM (in the schedule timezone)
*/15 * * * *    # every 15 minutes
0 0 1 * *       # first day of every month at midnight
```

<Aside type="caution" title="Day-of-month and day-of-week are ANDed">
Classic Vixie cron fires on _either_ when both are set. PAL Runtime requires both to match, so `0 9 1-7 * 1` fires on the first Monday of the month. If you port a crontab that relied on the OR behavior, rewrite it as two schedules. The search for the next fire time gives up after two years.
</Aside>

## Schedule API

### Create a schedule

```text
POST /v1/schedules
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "agentName": "research-agent",
  "cronExpr": "0 9 * * 1-5",
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "inputTemplate": { "mode": "daily-digest" },
  "deliveryEmail": "me@example.com",   // optional: email the result
  "enabled": true
}

Response: 201 Created
{
  "id": "sched-uuid",
  "agentName": "research-agent",
  "cronExpr": "0 9 * * 1-5",
  "inputTemplate": { "mode": "daily-digest" },
  "deliveryEmail": "me@example.com",
  "enabled": true,
  "nextFireAt": "2026-07-28T13:00:00Z"
}
```

### List schedules

```text
GET /v1/schedules

Response: 200 OK — bare array
[
  { "id": "sched-uuid", "agentName": "...", "cronExpr": "...", "enabled": true, ... }
]
```

### Update a schedule

```text
PUT /v1/schedules/{id}
Content-Type: application/json

{ "enabled": false }   // pause. Also accepts cronExpr, deliveryEmail, timezone
```

### Delete a schedule

```text
DELETE /v1/schedules/{id}

Response: 204 No Content
```

## Timezone handling

`timezone` is an optional IANA name (an invalid one returns 400). Cron then matches the schedule's local time. Resolution order: the schedule's zone, then `PAL_DEFAULT_TIMEZONE`, then UTC. With neither set, `0 9 * * *` fires at 09:00 UTC.

The deployment default (not a per-schedule zone) also sets the [budget](/docs/build/budgets/) day boundary: daily limits roll at local midnight in that zone.

## Example: weekday digest to Slack

`examples/daily-digest` is a workflow (GitHub open PRs, an AI step, a Slack post) on the schedule `0 9 * * 1-5` in `America/New_York`. Run `pal deploy` in that directory (the manifest carries the prompt and workflow), install the Slack and GitHub connectors, then post `schedule.json` to `POST /v1/schedules`. The response's `nextFireAt` is the next weekday 09:00 New York time.

The scheduler polls every 60 seconds, so a due schedule fires within a minute. To test without waiting for 09:00, set the row due (`UPDATE schedules SET next_fire_at = now() WHERE id = ...`) and watch `GET /v1/runs?agent=...`. The e2e suite does exactly this against fixtures (see [Testing](/docs/build/testing/)). An agent over its hard-fail budget does not fire at all, so an unattended schedule cannot run past its cap.

<Aside type="note">
Setting `deliveryEmail` also mails the run output. That path is not covered by the fixture suite.
</Aside>

## Surfaces trigger runs too

Inbound messages on a channel start runs. They are not schedules but follow the same run lifecycle. See [Surfaces](/docs/pal/surfaces/). Signed webhooks start runs as well; see [Webhook triggers](/docs/build/triggers/).
